title: NL coast: easy 50, flat, or walk
terrain: firm wet sand at the waterline, flat, no dunes today
coachNotes: OPTIMAL LOAD RULE, THE GOVERNING GATE FROM 24 AUG: a session passes only if it produces no symptoms during it, none immediately after, and none the next day. Any one of the three is a fail, and the next session drops back to the last level that passed. The ceiling during a run is 2/10 with no spike afterwards; mild is allowed, new or worsening is not. This replaces every softer wording elsewhere in this plan. GAIT, MEASURED FROM THE 22 AUG CADENCE STREAM ON 24 AUG. Your descent cadence is already good and is NOT the problem: 177 spm on grades steeper than -20%, 179 spm across the second half of the sustained descents, 176 on the final descent to the door. Do not change it, and do not let anyone tell you to. THE EXPOSURE IS FLAT AND SHALLOW DOWNHILL: 152 spm on flat ground and 156 spm at -3 to -10%. That is precisely the gradient band where the knee spends longest inside the 20-30 degree compression zone under load, it is the running you do most of, and the final 1250m into Bansko is full of it. TARGET 165-170 spm ON FLAT AND SHALLOW DOWNHILL, a 5-10% lift, which is the range the gait-retraining literature uses. Metronome or a 165 bpm playlist. Shorter steps at the same effort; do not convert it into more pace. STEP WIDTH: run slightly wider than feels natural, not on a tightrope. Narrow step width raises ITB strain and strain rate directly and it is one of the few things you can change inside 19 days. CUT 65 -> 55 AND SHORTENED AFTER THE 24 AUG ITB SIGNAL. If the band is quiet, easy 50 minutes flat. If there is any pin sensation at all, walk for an hour instead and lose nothing at all; CTL is 43 against a 42 target and this session cannot buy you anything. Flat only, no dunes, and mind the beach camber on the right side. FUELLING TARGET RAISED 60 -> 80 g/h ON 24 AUG. THIS SUPERSEDES EVERY 60 g/h TARGET BELOW. Products checked: Enervit Carbo Gel C2:1 Pro is 40g of carbohydrate per 60ml gel at a 2:1 glucose-fructose ratio, roughly double a normal gel, and the fructose clears the single-transporter ceiling that set the old 60 target. SiS GO Isotonic is 22g and maltodextrin only, i.e. glucose pathway only, 10mg sodium. GUT TRAINING ON ANY RUN OVER AN HOUR: 2 Enervit gels per hour, one on the hour and one on the half hour. WATER IS NOT OPTIONAL WITH THESE GELS: 40g in 60ml is about a 66% solution, strongly hypertonic, and taken dry it pulls water into the gut. 150-250ml of water with every gel. Do not stack a SiS gel on top of 2 Enervit, it is glucose only and pushes you past the ~60 g/h glucose ceiling without adding fructose. Transporter capacity adapts over roughly two weeks of repeated exposure, so this starts now or it does not happen before 5 September. Last day of the flat block, fly home tonight. Easy hour, nothing to prove. NO DUNES TODAY: Saturday took the vertical and the calves will know it, and a second sand-climbing day 48h apart two weeks out is how a new surface turns into an Achilles problem. Flat firm sand only. BEACH CAMBER: turn around every 10-15 minutes so the same leg is not on the low side for an hour, or run the flattest band above the high tide line. A canted surface is a documented ITBS provoker and it is the one avoidable risk on this beach. If the calves are sore from Saturday, run the road instead and lose nothing. GUT TRAINING: 60 g/h from minute 30, on this run too, easy or not. Transporter capacity adapts over roughly two weeks of repeated exposure, so every run over an hour between now and 5 September is part of the adaptation. Carbohydrate in the bottle rather than chewing your way there. Next weekend is the Alps and 5 September is the last specific day, so land Monday intact rather than fit.
